s1.syndrome_frame: Acute abdominal pain with peritonism and sepsis, complicated by respiratory failure
salient_findings: Multi-station mediastinal lymphadenopathy and pulmonary consolidation
key_facts: 60-year-old man with history of heavy cigarette smoking
History of emphysema, hypertension, and prostate cancer in remission
Presented with 4-hour history of acute right lower-quadrant abdominal pain
Fever (38.5°C), hypotension (systolic blood pressure 90 mmHg), and tachycardia (heart rate 110/min) on admission
Perforated appendix with collection and surrounding fat stranding on CT
Innumerable hepatic nodules and mural thickening of the cecum and sigmoid colon
Marked mesenteric, para-aortic, and portocaval lymphadenopathy
Pulmonary consolidation and collapse in the right lower lobe
Underwent exploratory laparotomy with subtotal colectomy and end ileostomy
Remained ventilated postoperatively
Failed extubation attempt on day 3

shortlist.label: Primary colorectal adenocarcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Patient had a thickened, woody sigmoid colon and innumerable hepatic nodules, suggesting possible colorectal cancer with metastasis

shortlist.label: Small cell lung carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Patient had a history of heavy cigarette smoking and presented with pulmonary consolidation and collapse in the right lower lobe, with bulky multi-station mediastinal lymphadenopathy on CT

shortlist.label: Sepsis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient presented with fever, hypotension, and tachycardia, and had peritonism and purulent contamination, indicating sepsis

shortlist.label: Peritonitis

raw.rationale: The patient presented with fever, hypotension, and tachycardia, which are classic signs of sepsis, and the presence of a perforated appendix with peritonism and multi-organ involvement supports this diagnosis
